clue.text: Gay old eccentric eager to return Cockney's fiver?

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or irregular, so the letters of the two words before it are rearranged
to return means the synonym for eager is read backwards

parts.note: eager means avid, keen

explanation.surface: A cheerful old oddball is keen to get back a Londoner's five-pound note.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang a Lady Godiva is a fiver, a five-pound note; the question mark flags the slang, and 'Gay old eccentric' reads as a person but is the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockney rhyming slang pairs the legendary naked rider's name with a five-pound note because the two rhyme.

clue.text: Farm animal, male, put in place for scientific research

indicators.note: put in means the letter for male is placed inside the word for the research room

parts.note: a lab, short for laboratory

explanation.surface: A farm animal, a male one, is sent to a laboratory for experiments.
explanation.definitionFit: A young sheep is a familiar farmyard creature.

clue.text: Party left public house with popular swimmer

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
PH is the map abbreviation for a public house, a pub
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A partygoer leaves the pub with a well-liked companion who swims.
explanation.definitionFit: The marine mammal is a famously graceful swimmer, so it is defined by what it does.

clue.text: Old fire engine in Dresden goes out after end of bombing

indicators.note: after means the rearranged letters follow the single letter in the answer
end of picks the final letter of the word bombing
out means the letters of Dresden goes are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A wartime picture: an old fire engine in Dresden heads out once the bombing ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' bombing gives G; 'out' shuffles DRESDEN GOES into REENGODDESS, which comes 'after' the G. Green Goddesses were British army fire engines kept as an emergency reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Green Goddess was the nickname of the Bedford emergency fire appliances, now retired, hence old.

clue.text: Collapse having crashed on trip

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a computer that has crashed is down
a trip is a stumble or fall

explanation.surface: Someone collapses after tripping and crashing to the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruin or fall from power is a collapse, as in the downfall of a regime.

clue.text: One maliciously damaging vehicle, youth going north

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a lad is a youth

explanation.surface: A young hooligan damages a van and heads off north.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who wrecks property deliberately is described by the phrase, a person of wanton destruction.

clue.text: Not as many to anoint? Bishop's not required

indicators.note: not required means the bishop's letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: to anoint is to bless with oil
B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A church question: fewer people to anoint, so no bishop is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Fewer or a smaller amount; the comparative of little stands in for not as many in loose usage.

clue.text: One of the Roosevelts confused one earl

indicators.note: confused means the letters of one earl are mixed up

explanation.surface: One of the Roosevelt family muddled up a member of the peerage.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleanor was the wife of President Franklin D Roosevelt and a famous First Lady.

clue.text: Musical instrument in grip on top of case

indicators.note: in a down clue on top of means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: to squeeze is to grip tightly
a box is a case or container

explanation.surface: A musical instrument is held in someone's grip, resting on its case.
explanation.definitionFit: Squeezebox is the informal name for an accordion or concertina, both played by squeezing bellows.

clue.text: Drink supplied by editor — I'm unwell, sickly, outside

indicators.note: outside means the scrambled letters go round the abbreviation for editor
sickly means the letters of the words before it are in a poor state, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A poorly editor is handed a hot drink to cheer them up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sickly' rearranges I'M UNWELL into MULLWINE, which goes 'outside' ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiced, heated red wine is a warming winter beverage.

clue.text: List of soldiers with unit initially

parts.note: men can mean soldiers, troops other than officers

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word unit

explanation.surface: A roll of soldiers with their unit noted at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill of fare, or the options on a screen, is a list of choices.

clue.text: Sailor tucking into biscuits, quality items

indicators.note: tucking into means the word for sailor is placed inside the word for biscuits

parts.note: crackers are crisp savoury biscuits
a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor eats biscuits, and they are first-rate ones.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'tucking into' as eating, but it is a container signal; a jack, or jack tar, is old slang for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackerjack is informal for something excellent, so the plural names first-class things.

clue.text: Keep away from car crash, having taken time off

indicators.note: having taken off means the letter for time is removed

parts.note: a shunt is British slang for a minor car collision, especially a rear-end bump

explanation.surface: Avoid a car crash by taking time off driving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes T from SHUNT, British slang for a minor car collision.
explanation.definitionFit: To avoid or steer clear of someone deliberately is to ostracise them.

clue.text: Country importing a Greek perfume

indicators.note: importing means the country takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: France is a country

explanation.surface: France imports a Greek perfume.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet smell or scent is what a perfume gives off, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: On which a duck may be recorded?

definitions.text: On which a duck may be recorded?

parts.words: On which a duck may be recorded?
parts.note: in cricket a duck is a batsman's score of nothing, and it is written on the record of runs; the surface suggests a birdwatcher's log

explanation.walkthrough: A duck in cricket is a score of zero, written down on the sheet that records the innings.
explanation.definitionFit: The sheet scorers fill in during a cricket match logs each batsman's runs, including a nought.

clue.text: Kiss and cuddle Charlie, a silly person

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a noodle is a fool

explanation.surface: Charlie, a bit of a fool, gets kissed and cuddled.
explanation.definitionFit: To smooch or neck amorously is to kiss and cuddle.

clue.text: Rare panic involving copyright

indicators.note: involving means the panic word wraps round the copyright letter

parts.note: a scare is a panic or fright
C, as in the copyright symbol, is its abbreviation

explanation.surface: An unusual panic over copyright.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in short supply is hard to find, which is what uncommon means.

clue.text: Fish in the morning up overlooking turbulent creek and lake

indicators.note: in a down clue overlooking means the first piece sits above what follows
in a down clue up means the letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: AM means in the morning, before noon

indicators.note: turbulent means the letters of creek are churned up

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: An angler is up early by a choppy creek and a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns AM into MA; 'turbulent' rearranges CREEK into CKERE.
explanation.definitionFit: The striped oily sea fish is a common food species.

clue.text: Live with rest, not posh

indicators.note: not means the letter for posh is removed

parts.note: the residue is the rest, what remains
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: Live a restful life, without any airs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' drops U from RESIDUE. U, as in 'U and non-U', is British shorthand for upper-class.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell or have one's home somewhere is to live there.

clue.text: Sales pitch about a new dog

indicators.note: about means the pitch word goes round the other letters

parts.note: a spiel is a glib persuasive patter

explanation.surface: A salesperson gives a pitch about a new dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The cocker or springer is a breed of gun dog with long ears.

clue.text: Battle station

definitions.meaning: the 1815 Belgian battle where Napoleon was defeated

explanation.definitionFit: The same name belongs to Wellington's famous victory and the London railway terminus named after it.

clue.text: Famous guitarist from LA — EP's unusual, extremely unusual

indicators.note: unusual means the letters of LA and EP's are put into an odd order
extremely picks the outside letters of the second unusual

explanation.surface: A record from Los Angeles by a famous guitarist is said to be truly odd.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'unusual' rearranges LA EP'S into LESPA; 'extremely' takes the outer letters of the second 'unusual', UL.
explanation.definitionFit: The American musician who pioneered the solid-body electric guitar has a famous Gibson model named after him.

clue.text: Snag involving base using the latest science?

indicators.note: involving means the snag word wraps round the letter for base

parts.note: a hitch is a snag or problem
E is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A problem at a base where cutting-edge science is used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' puts E inside HITCH. E is the base of natural logarithms.
explanation.definitionFit: Advanced technology is what the latest science applies, so the adjective fits loosely.

clue.text: Mates brought back put up with custard-pie comedy?

indicators.note: brought back means the friends word is read backwards

parts.note: pals are mates, friends
to stick something is to tolerate it

explanation.surface: Friends come back and endure a pie-in-the-face routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Boisterous physical humour with pratfalls and thrown pies is the classic knockabout style.

clue.text: No more than fair

definitions.meaning: merely or only, as in only a minute

explanation.definitionFit: The word works as an adverb meaning merely and as an adjective meaning equitable.

clue.text: Behind, in arrears

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the word arrears

explanation.surface: Behind with payments, owing money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the letters inside ARREARS; the surface reads 'in arrears' as one idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The back part of something, or one's bottom, is what behind means as a noun.

clue.text: Check strange diet

indicators.note: strange means the letters of diet are put into an odd order

explanation.surface: Someone queries a peculiar eating plan.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct or revise text is to check it over before publication.

clue.text: I must go in to protest at decline

indicators.note: must go in to means the letter I is placed inside the following word

parts.note: to deprecate is to express disapproval of, to protest at

explanation.surface: I have to go in and object to a falling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must go in to' puts I inside DEPRECATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose value, as a car or currency does, is to fall or decline.

clue.text: Informed team's leader, getting on in years

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter of the word team's

parts.note: someone getting on in years is old

explanation.surface: The team's ageing captain was put in the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Having been told something means one was given the news, so informed matches as a past participle.

clue.text: Vessel catching sole at sea for bulk trader

indicators.note: catching means the ship word goes round the scrambled letters

parts.note: a whaler is a ship used for hunting whales

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of sole are mixed up

explanation.surface: A ship catches sole at sea for a merchant selling in bulk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges SOLE into OLES, which WHALER is 'catching'.
explanation.definitionFit: A middleman who buys large quantities from producers and sells to retailers trades in bulk.
